title: 风（解落三秋叶）
author: 李峤
intro: A riddle-poem: the word “wind” never appears, yet every line shows what it does — tearing down autumn leaves, opening spring flowers, raising waves and bending bamboo.
analysis: 这首诗写风，可是全诗没有一个“风”字，像一个谜语。风是看不见的，诗人就写它做了什么：第一句，秋天它能把树叶吹落；第二句，早春二月它又能吹开花朵；第三句，吹过江面，掀起千尺高的大浪；第四句，吹进竹林，让成千上万根竹子都斜倒下来。前两句写风在不同季节的作用，一个“落”、一个“开”，一个让万物凋零，一个让万物生长；后两句写风的力量，“千尺”“万竿”是夸张的写法，让人感到风势很大。用看得见的东西来写看不见的风，这种从侧面去写的方法叫“侧面描写”。诗里还用了数字：三秋、二月、千尺、万竿，读起来很有节奏。这首诗简单好记，中国很多小学生都会背。
analysisEn:
This poem is about the wind, yet the word 风 never appears in it — it reads like a riddle. You cannot see the wind, so the poet shows what it does. Line one: in autumn it strips the leaves from the trees. Line two: in early spring it makes the flowers open. Line three: crossing a river, it raises waves a thousand feet high. Line four: blowing into a bamboo grove, it bends ten thousand stems.

The first two lines show the wind in different seasons, and they are opposites: one makes things fall (落), the other makes things open (开) — the wind can end life and begin it. The last two lines show its strength, with deliberate exaggeration in “a thousand feet” and “ten thousand stems”.

Describing something invisible through the visible things it affects is called cèmiàn miáoxiě, “indirect description”. The numbers — three autumns, the second month, a thousand, ten thousand — also give the short poem a strong, easy rhythm.

It is a perfect first poem: every word is simple, the picture is vivid, and it is fun to guess the answer before reading the title. Many Chinese children learn it in primary school.
background: Li Qiao (c. 645–714) was a high official and one of the most celebrated court poets around the time of Empress Wu. He wrote a whole series of short poems on single objects — sun, moon, wind, clouds — and this is the best known.
pronunciation: 万竿斜 的“斜”古音押韵读 xiá，今按普通话注 xié，网站采用 xié。三秋 sān qiū 指秋天（一说农历九月）。
version: 采用通行文本，全诗四句，无重要异文。

lines.lit: It can loosen and drop the leaves of late autumn;
lines.en: It shakes the autumn leaves from the trees,

lines.lit: it can open the flowers of the second month.
lines.en: and coaxes open the flowers of early spring.

lines.lit: Crossing the river — waves a thousand feet;
lines.en: Over the river it raises towering waves;

lines.lit: entering the bamboo — ten thousand stems slant.
lines.en: into the bamboo, and ten thousand stems bow down.

words.en: to loosen; to be able to
words.note: 这里有“能够”的意思，也有“使……脱落”的意思。
现代汉语“一日不见，如隔三秋”里指三年。
农历二月，大约是公历三月。
夸张；尺是古代长度单位。
现代汉语有“竹竿”“钓鱼竿”。

imagery.name: 风
imagery.zh: 全诗不出现“风”字，却句句写风：能落叶、能开花、能掀浪、能吹斜竹子。
imagery.en: The word “wind” never appears, yet every line is about it — dropping leaves, opening flowers, raising waves, bending bamboo.

imagery.name: 叶
imagery.zh: 秋风吹落树叶，写风让万物凋零的一面。
imagery.en: Autumn wind strips the leaves: the side of the wind that ends things.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 春风吹开花朵，写风让万物生长的一面。
imagery.en: Spring wind opens the flowers: the side of the wind that brings new life.

imagery.name: 竹
imagery.zh: 万竿竹子一齐倾斜，写出风的力量。
imagery.en: Ten thousand bamboo stems leaning at once show how strong the wind is.
